narrative:
The model determined that you have a 38% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the level of savings you have, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative account balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This negative status pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your lack of savings (unknown or none) was the second most important factor, but it actually worked in your favor. Most approved applicants also have very limited savings, so this commonality slightly reduced the model's concern about your risk.

The purpose of the loan being listed as "others" was the third most influential factor. This is an uncommon reason for borrowing—only 1% of approved loans fall into this category—which pushed the prediction toward denial.

Taken together, the negative checking account had the strongest negative impact, outweighing the modest positive effect from your savings situation and the negative effect from your loan purpose.

You should focus on building a positive checking account balance over the next few months, then reapply. This single change would likely improve your chances the most.
